svg.title: Who Sets the Bar on a DSCR or CRE File
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-dscr-underwriting-desk; chapter number: 11; chart type: org_architecture; title: Who Sets the Bar on a DSCR or CRE File; subtitle: The broker at the center of four underwriting tests; caption: DSCR is the gatekeeper metric, but the bar moves with the lender, the appraiser's rent schedule, and the debt-yield test.; assumptions note: Spokes group practitioners by the test they apply; thresholds are quoted as stated and differ by asset class and lender.; note: Sources are SEI Mortgage - Ryan Marks, Real Estate Finance Academy with Trevor Calton, Brandon Turner, Academy For Commercial Lending, and Tactica RES.; center: role: Commercial and DSCR loan broker; headcount: Broker of record; focus: Run DSCR at the broker's rent and at market rent, check debt yield, and back into the maximum loan before offering.; spokes: role: Small-balance DSCR lender; type: One-to-four and five-plus unit rentals (Ryan Marks); kpi: 600 credit floor on one-to-four; 680 credit, 25% down, 6 months reserves and 1.0 DSCR once past four units; role: Commercial underwriter; type: NOI-based sizing (Trevor Calton); kpi: $100,000 NOI over 1.25x caps debt service at $80,000 a year; role: Appraiser rent schedule; type: Market rent the lender actually uses (Brandon Turner); kpi: $11 per unit separated 1.19 from a 1.2 target on his duplex; role: Debt-yield test; type: Refinance survivability (Academy For Commercial Lending, Tactica RES); kpi: Paid CMBS sat at 13.3% to 14.4% versus sub-10% failures; one deal needed 60% LTV to clear a 10.5% bar
